title: PerfAnalyzer: Revealing Performance Trends using Version Oriented Visual Analysis of Scientific Software
problem: Understanding performance behavior of scientific software across versions and configurations is difficult. Tracking computational parameters, hardware settings, and outcomes across Git commits and multiple runs is complex, hindering root cause analysis of performance regressions.
motivation: Scientific software evolves through multiple versions. Performance changes correlate with code commits, but identifying which parameters drive changes is tedious with isolated measurements. Visual analysis across Git history could reveal performance trends and regressions.
method: PerfAnalyzer is an interactive dashboard that tracks how a program's performance changes as its code changes. It automatically gathers input parameters, hardware/software settings, and performance results at each code version stored in Git (the version control system), then displays this data visually so you can identify which code changes affected performance. The system was tested on CloverLeaf, a scientific computing mini-application, across multiple versions.
key_novelty: The core idea is displaying program performance alongside code changes across versions (tracked in Git), revealing which code modifications affect performance.
contributions: PerfAnalyzer dashboard for performance tracking across Git commits
Visual analysis enabling identification of performance-changing commits
Case study on CloverLeaf demonstrating effectiveness
Identification of performance issues difficult to spot in isolated measurements
limitations: Evaluation limited to single mini-application (CloverLeaf); scalability to full HPC applications unclear. Parameter collection and versioning overhead not quantified. Automated anomaly detection not discussed.
primary_theme: Version-oriented performance analysis for scientific software
